overall_structure.value: Partially recrystallized austenitic (γ) matrix in the 28Mn5Ni alloy after 50% cold rolling + 1173 K/1 h + water quench. The microstructure consists of relatively fine, equiaxed recrystallized austenite grains coexisting with retained deformed/strained austenite regions, prior B2 stringers (recovered to bamboo-type morphology) and newly precipitated fine intragranular plus intergranular B2 particles, together with fine intragranular κ-carbides.

unmapped_findings: TEM-EDS composition of B2 particles in the 28Mn5Ni alloy at 1173 K (Table 2, Fe balance): Particle-1 – Mn 16.5 wt% (14.9 at%), Al 14.2 wt% (25.7 at%), Ni 26.1 wt% (21.8 at%); Particle-2 – Mn 15.4 wt% (13.7 at%), Al 14.8 wt% (26.7 at%), Ni 27.5 wt% (22.8 at%). B2 is FeAl-based, contains significant Mn and Ni, and becomes enriched in Ni with increasing heat-treatment temperature (block b0042/b0054).

At HR+CR+1173 K, the Ni-containing alloys exhibited nearly identical but relatively lower strain-hardening exponent n (~0.30) compared to 28Mn0Ni (n = 0.50) at the same temperature, indicating lower strain-hardening ability of the Ni-containing LDS (block b0057).

For 28Mn5Ni, the recrystallization fraction at 1173 K (~0.4–0.5) was lower than that of the Ni-free alloy, and no noticeable growth of recrystallized grains occurred in Ni-containing LDS alloys up to 1173 K (Fig. 5a–b; block b0075).

Dual precipitation of intragranular B2, intergranular B2 and κ-carbides together with a partially recrystallized structure gave 28Mn5Ni a better strength (1.3–1.6 GPa) and ductility (17%) combination at 1023 K; at 1173 K there was a substantial drop in strength (block b0081).
